answer: A stake-weighted reputation bond resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can vouch for a new identity, and that deposit is slashed if the vouchee cheats. An attacker must pay the bond for every fake identity, so the cost scales linearly with the size of the attack, like an ocean rising against a shore, while honest agents earn the deposit back through good work. Trust then accrues slowly over many epochs, so an umber-dark newcomer cannot buy instant standing on a frozen tundra of shortcuts; it must earn attestations before its votes carry weight.
